questions.question: You’re running late for an important meeting. Your colleague says, *'I’m sorry I’m late, but my train was delayed by half an hour.'* How would you respond to show understanding and offer a solution?
options: That’s okay, but we should still leave now to catch up on the agenda.
I’m sorry you had to wait—we could start without you if that’s easier.
You’re always late, so it’s not a big deal.
I’ll make sure you get a lift to the station if you need it.
questions.answer: I’m sorry you had to wait—we could start without you if that’s easier.

questions.question: A friend suggests going to a museum tomorrow but you’ve already planned to visit a different attraction. What would be the most polite way to respond?
options: No, I don’t think museums are interesting—I’d rather go to the park.
That sounds great, but I’ve already got plans for the day.
I don’t like museums; I’ll just stay at home instead.
I’m sorry, but I can’t go—I’ve got a prior commitment.
questions.answer: That sounds great, but I’ve already got plans for the day.

questions.question: Your boss asks you to help with a presentation. You’re not sure if you’re available. What would be the most appropriate way to ask?
options: Yes, I’ll do it right away—I’m free this afternoon.
I’m not sure if I can help, but I’ll check my schedule.
No, I don’t think I can do that—I’m too busy with other tasks.
Could you send me the details so I can prepare properly?
questions.answer: I’m not sure if I can help, but I’ll check my schedule.

questions.question: At a formal dinner, someone says, *'I’m afraid I don’t understand your last point.'* How would you respond to explain it clearly?
options: That’s not important—I’ll move on to the next topic.
I’m sorry, I didn’t catch that—could you repeat it?
You’re wrong; I think you misunderstood me.
I’m sure you’ll get it next time—let’s not discuss it further.
questions.answer: I’m sorry, I didn’t catch that—could you repeat it?

questions.question: Your neighbour is struggling to fix a leaky tap. You offer to help, but they say, *'No, it’s fine—I’ll sort it out.'* How would you politely respond to encourage them to accept your help?
options: Don’t worry about it; I’ll just leave you to it.
That’s very kind of you, but I’d really appreciate your help!
You’re too polite—you should just ask someone else.
I’m sure you can manage—let’s not bother you.
questions.answer: That’s very kind of you, but I’d really appreciate your help!
